screening_decisions.reason: Not a qualitative study; systematic review of a trial. Not focused on home-based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation.
Qualitative study exploring family involvement in home-based exercise after stroke. Fits criteria: qualitative methods, home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative study on stakeholder preferences for a web-based physical activity portal for spinal cord injury. Relevant to telerehabilitation/home-based digital interventions.
Mixed-methods process evaluation of a home-based occupational therapy intervention for Parkinson's, including qualitative focus groups. Addresses home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative study on reasons for non-adherence to home- and centre-based cardiac rehabilitation. Explores patient experiences of home-based rehabilitation.
Systematic review of randomized controlled trials, not qualitative. Does not meet qualitative methods criterion.
Qualitative evidence synthesis on doctor-nurse substitution, not about home-based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation. Irrelevant topic.
Systematic review of clinical outcomes (quantitative studies). Not qualitative.
Grounded theory study on adherence to home-based inspiratory muscle training in COPD. Qualitative, home-based rehabilitation.
Mixed-methods study with qualitative interviews evaluating patient perspectives on home tele-rehabilitation for rheumatic diseases. Fits telerehabilitation.
Qualitative study on general rehabilitation experiences for traumatic hand injuries in rural areas, not specifically home-based or telerehabilitation.
Qualitative study to capture user needs for a home-based arm rehabilitation system post-stroke. Addresses home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative usability study of an asynchronous telerehabilitation platform for speech-language pathology. Fits telerehabilitation criteria.
Qualitative study exploring stroke survivors' experiences to design home-based robotic technology. Home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative evidence synthesis on digital communication for maternal/child health, not rehabilitation. Topic out of scope.
Systematic review of quantitative studies comparing care environments for rehabilitation. Not qualitative.
Mixed-methods feasibility study of telehealth home exercise for lung cancer; abstract lacks explicit qualitative data collection/analysis. Unclear if meets qualitative criterion.
Qualitative grounded theory study on care transitions from hospital to home rehabilitation after stroke. Home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative study on physical therapists' perceptions of patient adherence to home exercises for paraplegia. Home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative study on the impact of rehabilitation-in-the-home (RITH) on informal carers. Home-based rehabilitation.
Conceptual paper describing the CFIR framework, not a qualitative study on home-based rehabilitation. Out of scope.
Action research qualitative study developing a model for organization of home-based rehabilitation. Home-based rehabilitation.
Rapid review of rehabilitation needs due to COVID-19. Not a primary qualitative study.
Protocol for a future qualitative study on eHealth ethics, no results. Not a completed study.
Qualitative study of patient perceptions of telephone-delivered exercise therapy for knee OA. Telerehabilitation/home-based exercise.
Qualitative study on practice of support personnel in Norwegian reablement services (home-based rehabilitation). Home-based rehabilitation.
Development of a classification system (ICSO-R), not a study on experiences of home-based rehabilitation. Out of scope.
Pilot case series on telerehabilitation for TBI, primarily quantitative outcomes; no qualitative data collection described.
Cochrane systematic review of RCTs on telerehabilitation for low vision. Not a qualitative study.
Mixed-methods study including qualitative interviews exploring experiences of a home-telehealth programme for veterans with stroke. Home-based telerehabilitation.
Qualitative interview study on women's experiences of a web-based home intervention for chronic pain after rehabilitation. Telerehabilitation/home-based.
Qualitative phenomenological-hermeneutic study exploring patients' experiences of cardiac tele-rehabilitation; fits home-based telerehabilitation and patient perspective.
Not a qualitative study; a meeting report without data collection or analysis, and does not explore stakeholder experiences about provision of home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative interview study exploring stroke patients' experiences with home exercise programs and a novel home-based intervention; directly relevant to home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative study on stroke patients' transition from hospital to home after a home-based inpatient program (STRENGTH), exploring experiences and expectations; relevant.
The provided abstract describes an unrelated child health study (Growing Up in Australia), not home-based rehabilitation; does not meet any criteria.
Qualitative phenomenological study exploring lived experiences of burn survivors receiving home care, which includes rehabilitation; patient perspective on home-based services.
Qualitative content analysis study of caregivers' reasons for providing informal home-based stroke rehabilitation; caregiver perspective on home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative study exploring clinician perceptions of a wearable system intended to support patients at home during rehabilitation; aligns with home-based rehabilitation delivery.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of effectiveness, not a qualitative study exploring experiences or perceptions.
Focus is on nurse-caregiver communication in a web-based support intervention, not on the provision of home-based rehabilitation services; does not match criteria.
Qualitative case study examining factors enabling/constraining routine use of telerehabilitation; directly addresses organisation and delivery from multiple stakeholder perspectives.
Mixed-methods study with qualitative interviews evaluating a digital version of a home-based cardiac rehabilitation program; explores patient acceptability and experience.
Qualitative content analysis of patient experiences with video-based physiotherapy at home; a clear example of home-based telerehabilitation.
Mixed-methods evaluation including focus groups and interviews to assess an online cardiac rehabilitation program; patient perspective on telerehabilitation.
Mixed-methods study using qualitative interviews to identify barriers/facilitators to implementing a home-based CR program; directly relevant to organisation and delivery.
Explores mobility outcome preferences after post-acute inpatient/skilled nursing rehabilitation, not specifically about home-based rehabilitation provision.
Systematic review of effectiveness; not a qualitative study of stakeholder experiences.
Uses focus groups and think-aloud interviews to gather user requirements for a web-based home exercise program; addresses patient perspectives on a digital home-based rehabilitation program.
Methodology paper describing an approach to assess qualitative evidence syntheses; not a primary qualitative study exploring experiences.
Focus groups on preferred methods for PA information delivery, not about provision of home-based rehabilitation services.
Narrative review categorizing home-based programs; not a qualitative study.
Protocol for a Cochrane qualitative evidence synthesis, not a completed primary qualitative study, and not focused on home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative interview study exploring patient choices between home-based and hospital-based cardiac rehabilitation; directly relevant to factors influencing provision.
Cochrane review protocol on early discharge hospital at home; not a qualitative study.
Qualitative grounded theory study exploring how older adults collaborate with staff during home-based rehabilitation; directly relevant.
Mixed-methods usability study with qualitative component exploring user experiences of a home exercise app for people with disabilities; considered home-based telerehabilitation.
Cochrane protocol for a review of effects of home-based programmes; not a qualitative study.
The provided abstract discusses neurocysticercosis, a parasitic disease, completely unrelated to home rehabilitation; does not meet criteria.
Qualitative study on barriers to attending phase III outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, not home-based rehabilitation.
Book chapter providing an overview of telerehabilitation; not primary qualitative research.
Systematic review comparing outcomes; not a qualitative study exploring experiences.

Mixed-methods crossover trial that collected qualitative data via semi-structured interviews and sentiment analysis to explore patients' motivation and user experience with a home-based telerehabilitation app (HeartHab). Addresses patient experiences, meets qualitative component.

Mixed-methods study with semi-structured interviews exploring patient and practitioner experiences of a telerehabilitation model (urban physiotherapist via videoconferencing) for chronic back disorders. Qualitative data collected and analysed thematically.

The abstract describes a study on TB notification practices among private practitioners in India; no relation to home-based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation, and no qualitative exploration of rehabilitation service provision.

Retrospective mixed-method study with semi-structured interviews to identify barriers and facilitators to a home-based cycling programme in older patients with lumbar spinal stenosis. Qualitatively explores patient experiences of a home-based rehabilitation intervention.

Qualitative focus group study with patients, informal caregivers, and healthcare professionals exploring factors influencing uptake of eRehabilitation (telerehabilitation) in stroke care. Directly addresses stakeholder experiences and perceptions.
Cross-sectional quantitative study measuring sitting workspace using a Trunk-Support-Trainer in people with SCI. Not qualitative, not about home-based rehabilitation experiences.

Longitudinal qualitative study using semi-structured telephone interviews to explore older adults’ ongoing experiences of an internet-guided, self-managed vestibular rehabilitation (home-based telerehabilitation).
Not a research study; a meeting report/copyright notice with no qualitative data collection or analysis and no exploration of home-based rehabilitation provision.

Qualitative research with end-users (people with TBI) and therapists to design and test a home-based cognitive rehabilitation application using BCI. Explores user needs and experiences with a home-based telerehabilitation system.

Qualitative content analysis of open-ended questionnaire responses exploring lymphoma survivors' perceptions, preferences and barriers related to a home-based rehabilitation intervention. Addresses patient experiences.

Qualitative thematic analysis of data from therapists, engineers, and patients with hemiparesis on the use of a home-based virtual rehabilitation gaming system. Explores technological, communication, and training factors.

Qualitative content analysis of interviews with older people receiving home rehabilitation, mapping facilitators and barriers using the ICF. Directly explores older persons’ experiences of in-person home-based rehabilitation.

Realist evaluation using qualitative focus groups and home visits to understand how a home-based, technology-supported rehabilitation system (intelligent shoe) influences motor behavior. Explores patient and caregiver experiences.

The abstract presents a study on the validity of survey-based health-care utilization estimates in older adults. It does not concern home-based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation and is not about stakeholder experiences with such services.

Qualitative semi-structured interviews with patients and caregivers about their experiences performing caregiver-mediated exercises (a form of augmented home-based rehabilitation) after stroke. Explores roles, collaboration, and perceived benefits.

Focus group study with health professionals exploring their perspectives on collaborating with next of kin in reablement, a home-based, time-limited rehabilitation approach. Qualitative grounded theory analysis.

Mixed-methods formative study including semi-structured interviews with patients and health-care providers to understand needs and preferences for a mobile, home-based pulmonary rehabilitation program (telerehabilitation).

Qualitative study using feedback questionnaires and semi-structured interviews with persons with MS who completed a home-based exercise programme. Explores participant experiences and suggestions for future home-based rehabilitation trials.

Qualitative phenomenological study using interviews to understand older persons’ experiences of the rehabilitation process in their own homes after total hip replacement. Focuses on in-person home-based rehabilitation.

Focus groups with breast cancer patients to identify needs and preferences for a mobile app supporting self-managed upper-limb exercises at home (home-based telerehabilitation). Qualitative thematic analysis.

Qualitative interviews exploring mild-stroke survivors’ experiences of activities and participation after receiving home-based rehabilitation in an early supported discharge context. Addresses in-person home rehabilitation.
Cochrane systematic review of randomised controlled trials. Not a primary qualitative study; does not employ qualitative data collection and analysis.

Qualitative study using interviews and non-participatory observations to analyse care and rehabilitation processes post-discharge, focusing on patient participation and interactions with providers and next-of-kin. Explores experiences in the home-care context.

Qualitative arm of a pilot study that identifies barriers to community reintegration after SCI (e.g. mobility, insurance). Does not explore experiences related to the provision of a specific home-based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation service.

Qualitative study employing interviews and participant observation to describe COPD patients’ attitudes towards and experiences with a home-based tele-rehabilitation programme. Uses learning theory framework.

Case study with telephone interviews with patients and surveys of nurse mentors exploring experiences and delivery of a home-based, telephone-delivered cardiac rehabilitation programme. Includes qualitative perspectives.

Qualitative interviews examining the usability of a Nintendo Wii Fit home-exercise programme among adults with MS. Explores facilitators, barriers, and user experience with a home-based exergaming rehabilitation intervention.

Qualitative content analysis of semi-structured interviews with older adults about their experiences participating in reablement, a home-based, goal-oriented rehabilitation intervention. Identifies motivational factors.
Mixed-methods pilot RCT with qualitative evaluation (website questionnaire and interviews) of participants’ experience of a 12-week web-based physiotherapy programme (home-based telerehabilitation).

Descriptive qualitative study using semi-structured interviews to explore how older people maintain self-efficacy during home-based rehabilitation after orthopaedic surgery. Focuses on in-person home rehabilitation experiences.

Qualitative semi-structured interviews exploring patient experiences of a virtual (internet-based) cardiac rehabilitation programme. Addresses home-based telerehabilitation perceptions, benefits and barriers.
Not a qualitative study; investigates arterial stiffness in hypertension, not home-based rehabilitation service provision.

Qualitative observations exploring issues in providing technology support for a home telehealth service that included home-based rehabilitation; involves staff experiences relevant to service delivery.
Scoping review, not primary qualitative research.
Methodological review on literature searching, not about home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative focus groups exploring perspectives on pulmonary telerehabilitation, directly relevant.
Mixed-methods including qualitative interviews on patient experiences and barriers with home-based VR rehabilitation.
Systematic review of RCTs, not qualitative research.
Cochrane review, not primary qualitative study.
Review article, not primary qualitative research.
Perspective/commentary on teleophthalmology, not a qualitative study about home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative focus group study exploring healthcare providers' experiences developing a new interdisciplinary home-based everyday rehabilitation team.
Qualitative action research with interviews exploring service providers' perceptions and experiences of home-based rehabilitation.
Qualitative interviews with physiotherapists about their home-based stroke rehabilitation practice.
Qualitative interviews exploring clients' experiences of a multidisciplinary home-based rehabilitation program.
Focus is on mHealth for physical activity, not specifically on provision of home-based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation services.
Qualitative case study exploring interorganizational cooperation and professional experiences in a cardiac telerehabilitation program.
Qualitative content analysis of occupational therapists' narratives about ethical dilemmas in home-based rehabilitation.
Abstract describes a pediatric hearing screening study, not a qualitative study on home-based rehabilitation; title/abstract mismatch.
Explores caregivers' needs for heart failure self-management, not specifically home-based rehabilitation services.
Qualitative study exploring patients' perceptions of in-home telerehabilitation after total knee replacement.
Mixed-methods study exploring acceptability of telehealth consultation (including assessment/treatment) in patients' homes, relevant to telerehabilitation.
Qualitative focus groups/interviews with stroke survivors about their perceptions of a simulated rehabilitation technology, directly relevant.
Abstract is about clinical text classification with NLP, not a focus group study on eRehabilitation; title/abstract mismatch.
Qualitative interviews with clinicians about goal setting in stroke rehabilitation, including community/home settings.
Short overview/editorial without qualitative methodology; not a primary study.
Qualitative interviews exploring patient views and experiences of a home-based rehabilitation program.
Usability study collecting qualitative data on patient and physiotherapist experiences with a web-based rehabilitation intervention; relevant to telerehabilitation.
Qualitative phenomenological study of team members' experiences of home-based stroke rehabilitation.
Abstract describes a study on community-based health insurance, not home telehealth; title/abstract mismatch.
Mixed-methods with qualitative interviews exploring patient and clinician experiences of a home-based cardiac rehabilitation program.
Qualitative interviews exploring patient perceptions of a home-based cardiac rehabilitation programme with mentor support. Directly relevant.
Case report using semi-structured interviews to explore telerehabilitation via remote presence robot; includes stakeholder experiences of home-based service.
Systematic rapid living review; not a primary qualitative study.
Qualitative IPA study exploring experiences of home-based computerized cognitive training; addresses therapeutic alliance and stakeholder roles.
Qualitative case study with in-depth interviews examining the impact of managed competition on home-care rehabilitation services from provider perspectives.
Systematic review of RCTs on effectiveness; no qualitative methods.
Qualitative study using interviews to investigate patients’ and partners’ experiences of early supported discharge and rehabilitation at home after stroke.
Rapid living systematic review (Cochrane methodology); not a primary qualitative study.
Qualitative study with in-depth interviews exploring service and support needs during the transition from hospital to home for individuals with brain injury.
Mixed methods action research examining clinical perceptions of home telehealth video conferencing for rehabilitation; includes qualitative procedures.
Systematic review of barriers and facilitators; no primary qualitative data collection.
Observational study tracking smartphone app usage for cardiac rehabilitation; not qualitative in design.
Opinion/commentary proposing a fourth factor for evidence-based decision making; not an empirical qualitative study.
Pilot randomised controlled trial of a home-based prevention programme; not qualitative.
Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis to explore eHealth intervention requirements for home-based cardiac rehab.
Qualitative focus group study exploring therapists’ experiences of a home-based rehabilitation programme (STRENGTH) before hospital discharge.
Qualitative IPA study examining patients’ experiences and factors influencing choice between hospital and home-based cardiac rehabilitation.
Pilot descriptive study using interviews to explore caregiver experience with internet-based support; relevant to home-based stroke rehabilitation context.
Global burden of disease quantitative analysis; no qualitative methods.
Ethnographic fieldwork exploring how telemediated training at home becomes part of everyday life for COPD patients; qualitative.
Short editorial/commentary on maintaining essential rehabilitation services during COVID-19; not a qualitative study.
Qualitative study using thematic analysis of interviews to capture COPD patients’ perspectives on home-based pulmonary rehabilitation.
Book chapter describing the role of PRM in healthcare systems; not a primary qualitative research study.
Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis of female cancer survivors’ perspectives on remote physical activity support.
Multiple case study with realistic evaluation (qualitative design) of stroke patients’ use of feedback technology at home; abstract mismatch but title indicates relevance.
Systematic rapid living review; not a primary qualitative study.
Qualitative study interviewing people with motor neurone disease about their views on home-based e-Health/telehealth service delivery.
Interpretative phenomenological analysis exploring bodily experiences during a virtual (telerehabilitation) program after amputation.
Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews to explore physiotherapists’ perceptions before and after telephone-delivered exercise therapy.
Participatory action design with stakeholder focus groups (qualitative) to develop a home-based wheelchair skills program; captures user experiences.

The study is a randomized controlled trial reporting quantitative caregiver outcomes. Although it includes qualitative interviews, the primary design is not qualitative and the abstract does not present qualitative findings relevant to factors influencing service provision.

The study explores support needs of ARDS survivors across the illness trajectory, not specifically the provision of in‐person home‐based rehabilitation or telerehabilitation services. It does not focus on a defined home‐based rehabilitation program.

This qualitative study uses interpretive description methodology with interviews and a focus group to explore older adults' and health professionals' perspectives on loneliness during home‐based rehabilitation. It directly addresses experiences related to the provision of home‐based rehabilitation services.

The study investigates stroke survivors' needs for place attachment during rehabilitation, focusing on a conceptual framework rather than on the provision of home‐based rehabilitation services. It does not explore factors influencing service delivery.

This is a user‐centered design study aimed at developing a telerehabilitation platform. While it collects user requirements and usability feedback, the primary contribution is a design prototype, not a qualitative exploration of stakeholders' experiences of home‐based telerehabilitation services.

The study explores home care staff's experiences with assistive devices, not the provision of home‐based rehabilitation services. The focus is on assistive devices rather than on rehabilitation service delivery.

This qualitative analysis examines problems faced by new caregivers of stroke survivors enrolled in a web‐based intervention. The focus is on caregiving challenges, not on stakeholders' experiences of home‐based rehabilitation services.

This grounded theory study explores significant others' perspectives on how information and communication technology can support the rehabilitation process after stroke. It provides qualitative insights into the role of technology (potentially telerehabilitation) in rehabilitation, relevant to home‐based applications.

This qualitative process evaluation uses interviews and thematic analysis to explore stroke survivors' experiences of community rehabilitation with and without an integrated self‐management approach. It directly addresses perceptions of home‐based/community rehabilitation service delivery.

The study is a quantitative efficacy study of home‐based telerobotic‐assisted devices, reporting functional outcomes and cost analysis. It does not employ qualitative methods for data collection and analysis.

This pilot study uses structured questionnaires and semi‐structured phone interviews to evaluate end‐user perceptions of a telepractice application for home‐based swallowing therapy. It includes qualitative thematic analysis of patient experiences with telerehabilitation.

The study employs qualitative methods (interviews, participant observations, focus groups) to explore heart patients' and relatives' experiences with a gamified telerehabilitation program. It provides insights into factors influencing engagement and acceptance of home‐based telerehabilitation.

This qualitative study uses interviews and focus groups with health professionals to identify barriers and enablers of COPD telerehabilitation. It directly addresses factors influencing the implementation and delivery of home‐based telerehabilitation services from the staff perspective.

This mixed‐methods study includes semi‐structured interviews to explore patient experiences of a group‐based heart failure telerehabilitation program delivered via videoconferencing. The qualitative component provides relevant user perspectives on home‐based telerehabilitation.
This is a discussion paper proposing a conceptual description of rehabilitation services; it does not present primary qualitative research with data collection and analysis.

The study is a randomized controlled trial of early supported discharge with home rehabilitation, reporting quantitative outcomes and resource use. No qualitative data collection or analysis is described.

This qualitative study uses semi‐structured interviews and thematic analysis to investigate patients' and carers' experiences of Early Supported Discharge services, a home‐based rehabilitation model. It directly addresses experiences of the provision of home‐based rehabilitation.

This qualitative interview study explores patients' experiences of patient participation in a web‐based behavior change program combined with multimodal pain rehabilitation. It addresses experiences of a home‐based telerehabilitation intervention.

This qualitative study uses interviews with older adults to examine perceptions of interprofessional team caring skills in short‐term goal‐directed reablement, a form of home‐based rehabilitation. It directly addresses factors in the delivery of home‐based rehabilitation services.

The study explores user experiences of a mobile educational app for pressure injury prevention and management, not the provision of home‐based rehabilitation services. The app is an educational tool, not a telerehabilitation service, and the study does not address rehabilitation service delivery.

This study uses semi‐structured interviews to evaluate usability and acceptability of a mobile app prototype that delivers combined behavioural activation and physical rehabilitation at home. Qualitative themes report on patient and caregiver experiences of a home‐based telerehabilitation intervention.

This paper describes the development methodology for a personalised self‐management system for post‐stroke rehabilitation. It is a design/development paper and does not present a qualitative exploration of stakeholder experiences of service provision.
The study is a quantitative secondary data analysis examining trajectories of adherence to home‐based rehabilitation and its effects on physical function. No qualitative methods are used.

This is a Cochrane review of randomized controlled trials evaluating motor control exercise for acute low back pain. It is not a qualitative study and does not focus on home‐based rehabilitation service provision.

This qualitative study uses interviews with older adults to explore participation in daily activities within reablement (home‐based rehabilitation). It offers insights into factors influencing the experience and provision of reablement services.

This qualitative evaluation uses interviews to explore chronic pain patients' experiences with a personalised self‐management system used at home, which incorporates goal setting, feedback and therapeutic exercises. It provides insights into home‐based telerehabilitation.

The study explores nurses' perceptions of their role in rehabilitation within care homes (long‐term residential care), which is not home‐based rehabilitation as defined by the review (the person's own home).

This qualitative study examines patients' perspectives on postoperative physiotherapy education in the hospital and transition home. It does not specifically address the provision of home‐based rehabilitation services, focusing instead on patient education.
This is a report/editorial summarizing a webinar on the impact of COVID-19 on persons with disabilities. It does not present primary qualitative research with data collection and analysis.

This is an observational cohort study evaluating the feasibility and acceptability of telemedicine using quantitative service data and questionnaires. It is not a qualitative study and does not employ qualitative methods for data collection and analysis.
